response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.ordertune AS ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_relative_gap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rebate) AS baseline FROM g) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relative_gap, g.avg_rebate - b.baseline AS excess_over_baseline FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_rebate > b.baseline ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Rows with feerate = 0 produce a NULL relative gap (division guarded with NULLIF) and are ignored by the AVG of the gap; they still count in the average rebate.
The baseline is the unweighted mean of group-level average rebates across all groups (orderslink, ordertune), computed before filtering.
If orders.recordvault is not unique, fees would duplicate across joined orders; recordvault is treated as unique per order.
